owner_creation.analysis: src/brac.rs owns only match_brac stack scalars and a temporary function selector. It borrows the active input position through ch_seek/ch_get and allocates no local heap or descriptor.
owner_creation.invariant: The bracket scanner acquires no independent input owner.
limitations: The local clear disposition does not approve the active input subsystem.

aliases_escapes.analysis: src/brac.rs passes no retained data pointer to its reader selector; ch_tell returns a copied POSITION used by jump_line_loc. The selector carries no captured owner context.
aliases_escapes.invariant: A copied position does not become a reference to cached bytes.
limitations: Input/file stability remains a callee contract during this synchronous scan.

callback_targets.analysis: src/brac.rs assigns chget only ch_forw_get or ch_back_get, both with unsafe extern C fn()->c_int signature, before invoking it inside the scan loop.
callback_targets.invariant: The indirect target set is exactly the two named image functions.
limitations: This local target proof does not establish the native/provider contracts of other modules.

invalidation.analysis: src/brac.rs reads a fresh ch_tell coordinate for the successful bracket jump instead of retaining a buffer address across scanning. Failed endpoint lookup returns before reader selection.
invalidation.invariant: The scanner retains no byte pointer to invalidate after a seek.
limitations: Changing the active input outside this call is outside its local storage analysis.

mutation_commit.analysis: src/brac.rs updates only local nesting/count state, guards nesting increment at INT_MAX and calls navigation only after finding the matching close bracket.
mutation_commit.invariant: No partial heap-owner commit exists inside match_brac.
limitations: The public count argument and external navigation semantics are not requalified here.

release_pair.analysis: src/brac.rs must neither free input bytes nor close their descriptor: its interface exposes reader/seek/navigation calls and its return paths release only stack state.
release_pair.invariant: Borrowed input remains owned by the caller subsystem.
limitations: No source allocator pair is implied by the reader function pointer.

error_cleanup.analysis: src/brac.rs reports seek, missing-bracket and scan-end conditions then returns; there is no abandoned local allocation or callback context on those exits.
error_cleanup.invariant: Every local early return ends only stack lifetimes.
limitations: Error rendering can have independent owner/error obligations outside this file.

signals_handoff.analysis: src/brac.rs installs no handler and retains no shared mutable object of its own. M0-MEM-001 remains open for borrowed input/navigation owners; the local clear result provides no asynchronous caller approval.
signals_handoff.invariant: Synchronous stack-only scanning does not authorize owner replacement during a call.
limitations: No handler-to-bracket-scan mutation route is claimed by this record.

finding_context.M0-MEM-001: src/brac.rs keeps only stack scalars and a non-retained reader selector. M0-MEM-001 still governs the active input and navigation owners called by this scanner; clearing its local allocation/selector contract does not approve their raw shared state.
